note: Committed floor. run.mjs exits non-zero when a tracked metric falls below these by MORE THAN the 95% sampling margin for that metric at this n — not by more than 0.001, which was finer than the sampling error by three orders of magnitude and fired on one question. Raise it deliberately; never lower it to make a build pass, and record the reason in `reason` below.
reason: Full re-cut after the owner corpus rewrite, and a deliberate LOWERING of several floors rather than a gate-forced one: nothing here fired the regression gate. Every drop is inside the 95% sampling half-width at n=49 (BM25 hit@3 fell 10.2pp against a +/-12.7pp margin), which is exactly the slow-slide case the tolerance is documented not to catch, so the floors are re-cut by hand and every cause is listed here. (1) CORPUS. content/dist/content.json went 76 chunks to 70, 1101 terms to 1048, avgdl 43.3553 to 43.5429, manifest 4335 chars to 4246; corpus digest 053767a688866f9c to 9530564fdc07971c. Spetema was demoted from a case study to a notable project and keeps only project:spetema#summary; profile and facts prose was rewritten - fact:endurance went from 42 km. Marathon finisher. to I ran a marathon, profile:background lost the team size, and profile:background-statement is new. Both vector caches were rebuilt against the new digest, content/dist/vectors.json and evals/vectors.json, one billed Voyage run each, run once. (2) QUESTIONS. Seven ground-truth repoints, and no question added, removed or reworded: questionsHash is byte-identical at 001a02d3a171c99c and the denominators are unchanged at 49 retrieval / 16 abstention with every category and shape count identical, so this floor is measured on the same denominators as the last one and the movement is attributable rather than a denominator artefact. Five questions referenced the six dead Spetema ids (proj-spetema-ia, cross-b2b-b2c, cross-conflicting-audiences, metric-spetema-products, skill-motion); two more kept live ids that had lost the answer (metric-marathon, metric-team-size). One rule was applied to all seven and is recorded in the _corpusRewrite note in questions.json. NOTHING was recategorised as corpus-gap: the surviving Spetema summary still answers the layout, B2B/B2C and catalogue-size questions in as many words, so scoring them as abstention would have marked a correct retrieval wrong. (3) WHAT MOVED. bm25 hit@3 -10.2pp (0.7755 to 0.6735) is the largest single move and is exactly five questions: two are the Spetema repoints, whose only surviving target is now one card summary, and three are new losses to profile:background-statement, the reflective paragraph the rewrite added, which is now the BM25 top-1 result for six of its sixteen hit@3 misses because the index carries no stopword list and where (df 1), moment (df 1) and what (df 2) are therefore scored as rare, high-IDF terms. That is a retrieval finding for lib/knowledge/, not an eval defect, and this slice does not change it. embeddings hit@3 -4.1pp (0.9592 to 0.9184) is exactly two questions, both experience (exp-current, exp-studio-kipo), taking that class from 100% to 75%. tools-only, hybrid and tools-gated each fell 2.0-4.1pp on hit@3, and no arm abstention rate moved at all. Several metrics ROSE: bm25 ent@1 +6.1pp and hit@5 +2.1pp, gated-embeddings hit@1 +4.1pp and MRR +0.028, tools-gated hit@5 +2.0pp. (4) SIGNIFICANCE. embeddings vs bm25, the comparison that describes the shipped configuration, strengthened from 9-0 p=0.0039 to 12-0 p=0.0005, and it strengthened because BM25 fell, not because embeddings rose; embeddings fell too. gated-embeddings vs bm25 stays significantly WORSE than free BM25 (3-21 p=0.00028 to 5-18 p=0.0106), so the measured guardrail against re-enabling filtering inside search_content holds, on a smaller margin. bm25 vs tools-only LOST significance (19-6 p=0.0146 to 18-9 p=0.122): the margin still favours BM25 by 18.3pp but this question set no longer separates them, which weakens the claim the /evals prose makes in its first sentence.
